Container.Name: emby-watchparty-3
Container.Overview: Emby Watch Party 3.x, Director's Cut, for Emby and Jellyfin media servers. Guests watch together without media-server accounts, with their own audio, subtitles, quality, and HLS stream. Includes library search and filters, title details, synchronized playback, late-join voting, chat, and runtime administration. The :3 image stays on stable 3.x. This is a separate installation from the 2.x template, with its own appdata and host port. Production requires an HTTPS reverse proxy, explicit public origins, a stable session secret, and the current MEDIA_SERVER_* settings. Read the migration guide before moving an existing installation. GPU passthrough and hardware transcoding are configured on Emby or Jellyfin, which runs FFmpeg.
Container.Requires: A running Emby or Jellyfin server reachable from this container, a dedicated administrative API key issued by that server, and an HTTPS public URL routed to Watch Party. Generate SESSION_SECRET once with openssl rand -hex 32 and retain it. Set the public Web UI URL and matching CORS origin, and identify the reverse proxy's actual connecting address for TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS. Before first start, create the appdata directories and config.json containing {} as a file; keep existing configuration when migrating. Use one application worker. The :3 image must be published before installing this stable template. Deployment: https://github.com/Oratorian/emby-watchparty/wiki/Deployment-Unraid . Migration: https://github.com/Oratorian/emby-watchparty/wiki/Migration-to-3.0 .

Config.Name: Public HTTPS Web UI
Config.Description: Full public HTTPS URL for the Unraid Web UI launcher, for example https://watchparty.example.com or https://example.com/watchparty/. Include APP_PREFIX when used. The reverse proxy routes this URL to the host port below; the container itself serves HTTP. When retaining 2.x, use a different public hostname: ports and subpaths do not isolate session cookies.

Config.Name: Web UI Host Port
Config.Description: Published host port for Watch Party 3.x. Default 5001 avoids the 2.x template's 5000. Change this host value if needed; keep container port and WATCH_PARTY_PORT at 5000. Point your reverse proxy at this host port.

Config.Name: Media Server Type
Config.Description: Select the configured provider. MEDIA_SERVER_URL and MEDIA_SERVER_API_KEY must belong to that same Emby or Jellyfin server. Changing providers requires container recreation. Jellyfin playback uses HLS; progressive files, Live TV, and SyncPlay are outside the supported path.

Config.Name: Media Server URL
Config.Description: HTTP(S) media-server URL reachable from this container, for example http://192.168.1.100:8096. localhost means this container. A service hostname needs a shared Docker network with name resolution.

Config.Name: Media Server API Key
Config.Description: Dedicated administrative API key issued by the selected media server. Host usernames/passwords are entered through Watch Party, not here. Masking hides this field in the editor; server administrators can still read container environment values.

Config.Name: Session Secret
Config.Description: Stable signing secret of at least 32 characters. Generate once with openssl rand -hex 32 and paste the result. Keep it across updates; changing it invalidates signed cookies. Do not reuse a placeholder or leave it blank.

Config.Name: Session Cookie Secure
Config.Description: Production requires true and an HTTPS browser URL. HTTP between your TLS reverse proxy and this container is allowed. false is only for a separately configured development deployment.

Config.Name: Allowed Public Origins
Config.Description: Comma-separated public origins, for example https://watchparty.example.com. Include scheme and any nondefault public port, without a path or trailing slash. For https://example.com/watchparty/ use https://example.com. Production rejects blank values and *.

Config.Name: Behind Reverse Proxy
Config.Description: Declare whether a reverse proxy terminates viewer connections. Normally true for this HTTPS deployment, which requires TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS. Set false only for a genuinely direct topology; it does not remove production's HTTPS and secure-cookie requirements.

Config.Name: Trusted Proxy CIDRs
Config.Description: Required when Behind Reverse Proxy is true. Comma-separated CIDRs for the proxy's actual connecting address as Watch Party sees it, such as its Docker-network address. Use the narrowest relevant networks; do not trust all private networks or 0.0.0.0/0. Leave blank only for a direct deployment.

Config.Name: Deployment Mode
Config.Description: Production enables strict startup checks for secrets, secure cookies, explicit origins, proxy topology, and HLS token validation. Keep production for this stable deployment.

Config.Name: Container Bind Address
Config.Description: Keep 0.0.0.0 inside the container so the published port and reverse proxy can reach it. This is not the Unraid host address.

Config.Name: Container Port
Config.Description: Keep the container-side port at 5000. Change only Web UI Host Port to select a different published host port.

Config.Name: HLS Token Validation
Config.Description: Production requires true. This is a restart-required boot setting in 3.x, no longer an admin toggle. An old disabled config.json value is overridden by this environment setting.

Config.Name: App Prefix
Config.Description: Optional path such as /watchparty. Leave blank for a dedicated hostname. The proxy must preserve this prefix; include it in Public HTTPS Web UI but not in Allowed Public Origins.

Config.Name: Session Expiry (seconds)
Config.Description: Signed session-cookie lifetime, default 86400 seconds (24 hours). Use 1209600 to retain the former 2.x 14-day cookie lifetime. Active party state does not survive a process restart.

Config.Name: Application Data
Config.Description: Writable application data, including the avatar identity database. Use separate storage from a running 2.x installation; copy a stopped backup only as part of a deliberate migration.

Config.Name: Avatar Images
Config.Description: Persistent uploaded avatar files. Keep this paired with Application Data when backing up or migrating.

Config.Name: Admin Config (config.json)
Config.Description: Writable runtime settings file. Before a fresh installation, create this host path as a FILE containing {} if it does not exist. Do not use touch or let Docker create a directory. Preserve an existing config.json when migrating.

Config.Name: Logs (optional)
Config.Description: Optional persistent application logs. File logging and console levels are managed in /admin.
